scope: Corollary 2.8 (Point slicing after a fixed-label core) of the manuscript “Bochner–Riesz multipliers in three dimensions” (preprints/Bochner-Riesz-Multipliers-in-Three-Dimensions-September-24-2026/Bochner-Riesz-Multipliers-in-Three-Dimensions-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 078 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ea18d159eefcdc7f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 12-13. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. statement: Fix the values of some labels. On that fiber let ν be a retained probability law of a point P and free labels (Bj)j∈F , with ν ≤ AνP ⊗ O j∈F λj. The comparison laws λj may be the actual marginals obtained by a simultaneous core on this fiber. If Z = f(P), then on every positive Z fiber, ν(p, bF | Z = z) ≤ AνP (p | Z = z) Y j∈F λj(bj). 12 Thus the comparison label populations are those before the point slice, and any mass upper bounds already proved for them remain available. After a further restriction and core of conditional mass M > 0, each new actual label marginal is bounded by A/M times its respective λj.
